title: Gatta Kusthi 2 Arrives on Netflix Today After ₹56 Crore Box Office Run
excerpt: The Tamil sports comedy sequel starring Vishnu Vishal and Aishwarya Lekshmi begins streaming in five languages less than a month after its theatrical release.
body:
• Gatta Kusthi 2, the Tamil sports comedy starring Vishnu Vishal and Aishwarya Lekshmi, begins streaming on Netflix on July 31, 2026.
  • The film will be available in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam, making it accessible to audiences across India and the diaspora.
  • After a theatrical run that began July 3, the sequel grossed an estimated ₹56 crore worldwide — a career milestone for lead actor Vishnu Vishal.
  • Critics gave the film mixed reviews, though family audiences drove strong ticket sales throughout its four-week run.

Gatta Kusthi 2, the sequel to the 2022 Tamil sports comedy drama, premieres on Netflix today, July 31, wrapping up a theatrical window of just under four weeks. The film stars Vishnu Vishal and Aishwarya Lekshmi reprising their roles as Veera and Keerthi, and will stream in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=18HeyuDeLbY

The makers confirmed the OTT date on social media with a promotional caption in Tamil — "Indha round 2 la kadhal ah? Illa kusthi ah?" (In Round 2, is it romance or a showdown?) — signaling the film's continued focus on blending relationship drama with wrestling action.

A ₹56 Crore Theatrical Run

Released on July 3, 2026, Gatta Kusthi 2 was distributed in Tamil Nadu by Red Giant Movies and performed steadily at the box office. The film crossed ₹30 crore worldwide within its first week and hit ₹44.5 crore by day 10. On July 22, Vishnu Vishal confirmed the film had crossed the ₹55 crore mark — the first time any of his films reached the ₹50 crore milestone. According to tracking site Cineulagam, the film ended its theatrical run at approximately ₹56 crore worldwide.

The numbers represent a significant step up for Vishal, who has built a steady career in Tamil cinema but had not previously delivered a blockbuster of this scale.

Role Reversal at the Heart of the Sequel

Directed by Chella Ayyavu, who also helmed the original, the sequel picks up several years after the first film. Keerthi now works for Indian Railways under the sports quota while training for national-level wrestling championships. Veera has embraced the role of a stay-at-home husband, managing the household and raising their six-year-old daughter, Mathi Malar.

The couple's dynamic shifts when parenting disagreements surface — Keerthi wants Mathi to follow her into wrestling, while Veera supports their daughter's passion for dance. A manipulative wrestling coach exploits Veera's insecurities, setting off a chain of events that threatens Keerthi's career and pushes the couple toward divorce. The 154-minute film builds to a wrestling showdown that doubles as a reckoning for the marriage.

The supporting cast includes Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, Karunas, Munishkanth, Kaali Venkat, and child actor Zara Zyanna as Mathi Malar. Sean Roldan composed the music, with cinematography by KM Bhaskaran.

Mixed Reviews, Strong Audience Reception

Critics were divided on the film. Bhuvanesh Chandar of The Hindu called it an improvement over its predecessor with "sharper writing" but noted it "repeats its biggest mistakes when it matters most." M. Suganth of The Times of India was less generous, writing that "the premise does have potential" but calling the execution "convenient and predictable."

"Gatta Kusthi 2 comes together well mainly because the screenplay has long gags that you warm up to."

— Avinash Ramachandran, Cinema Express

Janani K of India Today gave the film 2 out of 5 stars, criticizing its gender politics. Despite the critical divide, family audiences turned up consistently — the film sold over 31,000 tickets on BookMyShow in a single 24-hour window during its second week.

What's Next for the Team

Vishnu Vishal and Chella Ayyavu are already confirmed to reunite for a new family entertainer. The project, tentatively titled VVS11, was reported on July 23, riding the commercial momentum of Gatta Kusthi 2's success. Meanwhile, Aishwarya Lekshmi has a Netflix series, #Love, a Tamil romantic comedy co-starring Arjun Das, currently in post-production.

For diaspora audiences who missed the theatrical window, the Netflix debut makes Gatta Kusthi 2 immediately accessible — no hunting for niche OTT platforms required. The film joins a growing slate of mid-budget Tamil hits making the theater-to-streaming jump in under a month.
nri_angle: Streaming in five languages on Netflix, the film is immediately accessible to Indian diaspora audiences worldwide who missed its theatrical run in India.
